reading: and will be to [[name:Ααρων]] [[in the serving public offices at one's own cost|within, inside of, and by means of the serving public offices at one's own cost, the performing public duties and serving the people and state, the serving, the performing religious service and ministering|ἐν; λειτουργέω]] [[heard|heard and audible, that should be heard|ἀκουστός]] [[the sound|the sound and tone, the sound of the voice, the cry, the faculty of speech and discourse, the language, the saying|φωνή]] of him [[to going into|to going into, to entering, to coming upon, to coming into court, to entering on, to coming into one's mind|εἴσειμι]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the devoted to the gods|the devoted to the gods and sacred and holy, the holy and pure|ἅγιος]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of and before, opposite and face to face, against|ἐναντίον]] [[of lord|of lord / master, of the head, of master, of the Lord, of Jehovah|κύριος]] and [[to going out|to going out and coming out, to leaving, to coming forth, to marching out with an army, to going out on, to coming forward on the stage, to coming to an end and expiring|ἔξειμι]], [[that|that, in order that|ἵνα]] [[not|not, that not, perhaps, surely not and you don't mean to say that|μή]] [[may die off|may die off and die, may be put to death and slain|ἀποθνήσκω]]. —

greek: καὶ ποιήσεις πέταλον χρυσοῦν καθαρὸν καὶ ἐκτυπώσεις ἐν αὐτῷ ἐκτύπωμα σφραγῖδος Ἁγίασμα κυρίου.
hint: A gold plate is engraved like a seal with 'Holiness of the Lord'.

notes.text: ἐκτύπωμα, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's figure in relief, reflection.
The inscription, capitalised as speech is; ἁγίασμα, holy place, sanctuary, holiness.

reading: and [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create|ποιέω]] [[a leaf|a leaf, a leaf of metal|πέταλον]] [[golden|golden, of gold, decked and inlaid with gold, gilded and gilt, gold-coloured and golden-yellow|χρυσοῦς]] [[clear of dirt|clear of dirt and clean and spotless and unsoiled, clear and open and free, clear from shame and pollution and pure, clear of guilt and defilement and clean and pure, purified, clear of and from, clear of admixture and clear and pure, pure and genuine, without blemish, clear and exact|καθαρός]] and [[you will model|you will model, you will work in relief|ἐκτυπόω]] [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to it [[figure in relief|figure in relief, reflection|ἐκτύπωμα]] [[of a seal|of a seal and signet and seal-ring, of gem and stone for a ring, of impression of a signet-ring and seal|σφραγίς]] [[holy place|holy place and sanctuary, holiness|ἁγίασμα]] [[of lord|of lord / master, of the head, of master, of the Lord, of Jehovah|κύριος]].

greek: καὶ ἐπιθήσεις αὐτὸ ἐπὶ ὑακίνθου κεκλωσμένης, καὶ ἔσται ἐπὶ τῆς μίτρας· κατὰ πρόσωπον τῆς μίτρας ἔσται.
hint: It is tied on with blue cord to the front of the turban.

notes.text: ὑάκινθος feminine, by its participle, as at 28:5.
μίτρα, a belt or girdle, a head-band, a Persian head-dress, turban; the description's beneath and over set aside.

greek: καὶ ἔσται ἐπὶ τοῦ μετώπου Ααρων, καὶ ἐξαρεῖ Ααρων τὰ ἁμαρτήματα τῶν ἁγίων, ὅσα ἂν ἁγιάσωσιν οἱ υἱοὶ Ισραηλ, παντὸς δόματος τῶν ἁγίων αὐτῶν· καὶ ἔσται ἐπὶ τοῦ μετώπου Ααρων διὰ παντός, δεκτὸν αὐτοῖς ἔναντι κυρίου. —
hint: On Aaron's forehead it takes away the faults in Israel's holy gifts.

notes.text: ἐξαίρω, to lift up, lift off; ἐξαείρω is the entry's heading.
δεκτός, acceptable, one translation, plain text.

reading: and will be [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] [[of the space between the eyes|of the space between the eyes and brow and forehead, of the front and face|μέτωπον]] of [[name:Ααρων]], and [[will lift up|will lift up and lift off the earth, will raise in dignity and exalt, will raise and arouse and stir up, will carry off for himself and earn and win and gain, will take on himself|ἐξαίρω]] [[name:Ααρων]] [[the failures and faults and sins|the failures and faults and sins, the bodily defects and maladies|ἁμάρτημα]] [[of the devoted to the gods|of the devoted to the gods and sacred and holy, of the holy and pure|ἅγιος]], [[as great as|as great as, as much as, as far as, as long as, as many as|ὅσος]] ever [[may hallow|may hallow and make sacred|ἁγιάζω]] the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]], [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single|πᾶς]] [[of gift|of gift, of payment|δόμα]] [[of the devoted to the gods|of the devoted to the gods and sacred and holy, of the holy and pure|ἅγιος]] of them; and will be [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] [[of the space between the eyes|of the space between the eyes and brow and forehead, of the front and face|μέτωπον]] of [[name:Ααρων]] [[through|through, right through, by means of, by the agency of|διά + genitive]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single|πᾶς]], acceptable to them in the presence of [[of lord|of lord / master, of the head, of master, of the Lord, of Jehovah|κύριος]]. —

greek: καὶ οἱ κόσυμβοι τῶν χιτώνων ἐκ βύσσου· καὶ ποιήσεις κίδαριν βυσσίνην καὶ ζώνην ποιήσεις, ἔργον ποικιλτοῦ.
hint: The tunic's fringes are of linen; a linen turban and an embroidered sash follow.

notes.text: κόσυμβος, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's fringe, citing 28:35 by another numbering, and hair-net.

reading: and [[the fringes|the fringes, the hair-nets|κόσυμβος]] [[of the garments worn next the skin|of the garments worn next the skin and frocks, of the coats of mail, of the coverings, of the skins|χιτών]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of a fine flax|of a fine flax, of linen made from it|βύσσος]]; and [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create|ποιέω]] [[Persian head-dress|Persian head-dress, turban of Jewish high priest, an Arcadian dance|κίδαρις]] [[made of byssus (βύσσος)|made of byssus (βύσσος), fine linen|βύσσινος]] and [[belt and girdle|belt and girdle, lower girdle worn by women above the hips, man's belt, part round which the girdle past and waist and loin|ζώνη]] [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create|ποιέω]], [[work|work, business, deeds, action, works of industry and tilled lands|ἔργον]] of a broiderer.

greek: καὶ τοῖς υἱοῖς Ααρων ποιήσεις χιτῶνας καὶ ζώνας καὶ κιδάρεις ποιήσεις αὐτοῖς εἰς τιμὴν καὶ δόξαν.
hint: Aaron's sons get tunics, sashes and caps, for honour and glory.

notes.text: κίδαρις, the plural, LSJ's head-dresses, turbans.

greek: καὶ ἐνδύσεις αὐτὰ Ααρων τὸν ἀδελφόν σου καὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ μετʼ αὐτοῦ· καὶ χρίσεις αὐτοὺς καὶ ἐμπλήσεις αὐτῶν τὰς χεῖρας καὶ ἁγιάσεις αὐτούς, ἵνα ἱερατεύωσίν μοι.
hint: Aaron and his sons are to be clothed, anointed, ordained and consecrated.

notes.text: You will fill their hands, the Hebrew's idiom for ordination, said in Greek word for word.
χρίω, to touch on the surface, to rub or anoint; the middle's and the passive's left out.

reading: and [[you will clothe in|you will clothe in, you will clothe|ἐνδύω]] them [[name:Ααρων]] [[the son of the same mother|the son of the same mother, the brother, the near kinsman|ἀδελφός]] of you and the sons of him [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of him; and [[you will touch on the surface|you will touch on the surface and rub and anoint with scented unguents, you will infect, you will rub over with colour, you will wound on the surface and prick and sting|χρίω]] them and [[you will fill quite full|you will fill quite full, you will fill full of|ἐμπίπλημι]] of them [[the hands|the hands, the hands and arms, the arms|χείρ]] and [[you will hallow|you will hallow and make sacred|ἁγιάζω]] them, [[that|that, in order that|ἵνα]] may be priests to me.

greek: καὶ ποιήσεις αὐτοῖς περισκελῆ λινᾶ καλύψαι ἀσχημοσύνην χρωτὸς αὐτῶν· ἀπὸ ὀσφύος ἕως μηρῶν ἔσται.
hint: Linen drawers cover their nakedness from loins to thighs.

λινοῦς, filed in Middle Liddell under λίνεος, of flax, flaxen, linen.

greek: καὶ ἕξει Ααρων αὐτὰ καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ, ὡς ἂν εἰσπορεύωνται εἰς τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ μαρτυρίου ἢ ὅταν προσπορεύωνται λειτουργεῖν πρὸς τὸ θυσιαστήριον τοῦ ἁγίου, καὶ οὐκ ἐπάξονται πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς ἁμαρτίαν, ἵνα μὴ ἀποθάνωσιν· νόμιμον αἰώνιον αὐτῷ καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ μετʼ αὐτόν.
hint: They wear these at the tent and the altar, so as not to incur guilt; a statute for all time.

notes.text: ἐπάγω, the future middle: the middle's senses, to procure, to bring upon oneself, the active's left to the active.
The tent of the testimony, for the Hebrew ʾōhel môʿēd, the tent of meeting.
